### **1. Demand for platinum** 

- _Our estimates of platinum demand have been downgraded across the forecast period, reflecting subdued demand in autocatalysts until 2011 and weaker activity in industrials. Jewellery remains elevated and retail investment has been upgraded but these are not sufficient to prevent lower overall demand estimates than previously indicated._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|3,814|2,926|3,076|3,480|
|Jewellery|1,646|2,038|2,120|2,242|
|_Chemical_|346|291|330|384|
|_Electronics_|378|308|305|319|
|_Glass_|441|95|204|468|
|_Petroleum_|200|185|171|167|
|_Retail investment_|452|382|270|190|
|_Other_|456|389|412|460|
|Industrial & others|2,273|1,650|1,691|1,988|
|**Total**|**7,734**|**6,614**|**6,887 **|**7,710**|



### **1.1  Autocatalyst** 

- Following a major review, our assumptions for autocatalyst demand now call for an 18% decline in global light vehicle production in 2009 with improvements of 10% and 12% in 2010 and 2011 respectively.  However, this includes the view that following a 19% drop this year, European light vehicle production will stagnate in 2010 as the boost from this year’s scrappage programmes unwinds.  As a result, the recovery in Europe’s auto industry is deferred until 2011. 

- The critical issue for platinum is diesel and its elevated share of European light vehicle production – 48% last year.  Although Europe’s high profile scrap incentive programmes tend to favour smaller, generally gasoline vehicles, diesel’s share of passenger car registrations remained at 46% for the first five months of 2009, despite a major decline in Germany where diesel’s share dropped to 30%.  Adding in light com

mercial vehicles, the majority of which are diesel, we are assuming only a marginal decline in diesel’s share of production share this year (to 47%) and expect this to rise only modestly thereafter. 

### **1.2 Jewellery** (reported as gross fabrication) 

- We have moderated our estimates for platinum in jewellery, although our forecast of a strong recovery in 2009 and continuing growth thereafter remain.  This is predicated on our view that prices, although firmer in recent weeks, will remain conducive for elevated consumption, especially in the key market of China. 

### **1.3 Industrial & other applications** 

- After a detailed reassessment, we have lowered our forecasts for demand in a number of sectors, although glass (which is set for a major fall this year) is unchanged.  Some offset to this has emerged in retail investment which has been surprisingly resilient this year, encouraging us to raise our forecasts for 2010 and 2011 (although our view of a downward trend from last year’s record high remains).

### **2. Demand for palladium** 

- _We have raised our estimates for demand in autocatalyst and industrial applications. However, much of this is offset a scaling back in jewellery.  Overall, we see demand as similar in 2009 but somewhat higher in 2010 and 2011 by comparison with our previous forecast._ 

|**Palladium 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|4,408|3,559|4,147|4,725|
|Jewellery|1,301|1,323|1,437|1,507|
|_Dental_|776|742|730|717|
|_Chemical_|385|304|333|390|
|_Electronics_|1,347|1,265|1,385|1,540|
|_Retail investment_|84|205|85|58|
|_Other_|91|76|86|93|
|Industrial & others|2,683|2,592|2,619|2,798|
|**Total**|**8,391**|**7,474**|**8,203**|**9,030**|



### **2.1 Autocatalyst** 

- We have upgraded our view of palladium in autocatalyst following revisions to the outlook for global vehicle production.  After this year’s heavy decline, our forecast 10% improvement in vehicle production in 2010 will be strongly biased to gasoline vehicles and hence favour palladium, with European production unlikely to grow.  Palladium demand is expected to gather momentum in 2011 when Europe is expected to recover strongly, joining a broad based improvement in global vehicle production.  Meanwhile, palladium will benefit from substitution versus platinum, as its role in diesel increases. 

### **2.2 Jewellery** (reported as gross fabrication) 

- We have lowered our estimate for palladium in jewellery in 2009, with the effect of this flowing though into 2010 and 2011.  China remains the principal market and recent contact with trade sources, although mixed, point to the likelihood of little change in demand this year.  However, we are fairly confident that palladium will register steady, if unexciting gains in 2010 and 2011, mainly in China but with useful support from other markets. 

### **2.3 Industrial** 

- Our forecasts have been

upgraded for industrials in total.  This is mainly due to an improved outlook for electronics.  In many areas of consumer electronics, the severe declines of late 2008/early 2009 have been followed by a stronger than expected rebound (in some cases causing a temporary shortages of key materials).  We believe this will continue as the global economy improves and functionality demands increase still further.

### **3. Supply** 

### **3.1  Platinum supply** 

- _With reduced estimates for mine production and autocatalyst recycling, we expect a greater reduction in overall platinum supply in 2009 than previously envisaged.  Following a return to growth in South African production in 2010 and a return to trend in autocatalyst recycling, we expect platinum supply in total to top 8m ounces in 2011._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Mineproduction:**|||||
|South Africa|4,671|4,474|4,707|5,142|
|Russia|835|799|792|786|
|Canada|227|204|268|276|
|United States|115|113|92|80|
|Zimbabwe|180|194|250|300|
|Others|123|112|109|109|
|**Total mineproduction**|**6,150**|**5,896**|**6,218**|**6,694**|
|Autocatalyst recycling|998|784|1,051|1,174|
|Jewelleryscrap|910|299|266|261|
|**Total supply**|**8,058**|**6,979**|**7,535**|**8,129**|



- We have altered our view of platinum production from South Africa in 2009 and now visualise a moderate decline.  This is due to slower progress in the junior sector in bringing a number of new mines into production, together with a litany of individually minor but collectively significant difficulties among the country’s major established mines.  Although we remain of the view that South Africa will return to growth from 2010, we have scaled back our estimates following the abandonment by Anglo Platinum of its 5% annual growth target, replaced by a steady‐state objective of 2.5m ounces per annum with upside potential should the market require it (which we do not believe it will over this forecast period). Meanwhile, we now have a more optimistic view on Zimbabwe’s prospects for achieving greater production growth from 2010. 

- Having signalled a decline in autocatalyst recycling volumes in our previous report, we believe the outlook for 2009 is somewhat worse than we visualised.  Although the various scrap incentive programmes now in existence will add to the number of old vehicles available for recycling, volumes in total remain subdued by comparison with more normal levels and the incentive for recycling is much diminished since 2007 and early 2008. However, there is a build‐up of unprocessed material at the breakers yards and this should aid a recovery to near normal levels from 2010. 

- Following an in‐depth review, we have made slight alterations to supply from jewellery scrap in 2010 and 2011, while our estimate for 2009 remains unchanged.  In terms of the decline in overall supply in 2009, this year’s fall

in jewellery scrap recycling (after the exceptional high of 2008) remains the biggest single factor.

**Market Parameters Report – August 2009** 





### **3.2  Palladium supply** 

- _Palladium supply is similarly impacted by our reassessment of both South African mine and autocatalyst recycling.  Accordingly, we have scaled back our estimates for overall supply in 2009 and 2010 but visualise slightly higher level in 2011 than previously indicated._ 

|**Palladium 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Mineproduction:**|||||
|South Africa|2,366|2,370|2,559|2,864|
|Russia|2,712|2,600|2,600|2,600|
|Canada|524|308|369|373|
|United States|384|374|304|268|
|Zimbabwe|139|152|199|238|
|Others|254|250|245|245|
|**Total mineproduction**|**6,379**|**6,053**|**6,276**|**6,589**|
|Autocatalyst recycling|1,184|926|1,278|1,743|
|Jewelleryscrap|195|131|140|155|
|**Total supply**|**7,758**|**7,110**|**7,695**|**8,487**|



- Although we have downgraded our expectations for South Africa’s underlying production, its palladium output in 2009 will be supplemented by the release of accumulated pipeline. Thereafter, palladium output broadly tracks platinum production and is aided by improving production in Zimbabwe.  However, with Russia’s production expected to stabilise at 2.6m ounces from 2009, total supply from mine production in 2011 is visualised at only 3% higher than the level achieved in 2008.  This compares with a 9% rise in platinum mine production between the same two points. 

- As with platinum, the recovery of palladium from autocatalyst recycling will decline sharply in 2009 but should recover to near normal levels in 2010, getting fully back on track by 2011. Meanwhile, although we have revised our estimates for jewellery scrap, this remains a relatively minor component of overall palladium supply.

### **4. Market balances** 

### **4.1 Platinum** 

- _We remain of the view that platinum will register a substantial gross surplus in 2009 and 2010 but now see 2011 as a further year of significant gross surplus, with supply having increased and demand, although much improved, below our previous estimate._ 

- _Our projections for ETF inflows are essentially unchanged with the result that the market is closer to balance at the residual level in 2009 but still registers a large surplus in 2010 and 2011.  We have yet to include estimates for recently launched ETFs in Japan (only days ago) and a possible listing in the United States (which remains at the application stage, although will likely be successful if approved)._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|New supply|8,058|6,979|7,535|8,129|
|Fabrication demand|7,734|6,614|6,887|7,710|
|**_Gross surplus(deficit)_**|**324**|**364**|**648**|**419**|
|ETF demand|(102)|(275)|(160)|(120)|
|**Residual surplus(deficit)**|**222**|**89**|**488**|**299**|

### **4.2 Palladium** 

- _With various adjustments to supply and demand, the picture for palladium is of significant gross surplus over the forecast period.  The most significant change here is in 2009, with our previous report having suggested the likelihood of a closely balanced market at this level._ 

- _While we may be closer to the time when Russian stock sales no longer overshadow the palladium market, we expect selling to continue over the forecast period and have taken the prudent approach of raising our expectations for sales in 2010 and 2011.  At the levels indicated, these sales will be only partly absorbed by the recurring gross deficits and continuing positive inflows to the existing ETF, leaving investors in palladium futures and the OTC market to absorb an ongoing residual surplus.  As with platinum, our estimates for ETFs are confined to the established funds and no provision has yet been made for funds in Japan or a potential listing in the US._

|---|---|---|---|---|
|New supply|7,758|7,110|7,695|8,487|
|Fabrication demand|8,391|7,474|8,203|9,030|
|**_Gross surplus(deficit)_**|**(634)**|**(364)**|**(509)**|**(543)**|
|Russia stock sales|1,280|1,300|1,300|1,300|
|ETF demand|(381)|(330)|(150)|(100)|
|**Residual surplus(deficit)**|**265**|**606**|**641**|**657**|

### **5. Above‐ground stocks** 

- _Above‐ground stocks are implied from historical trade data for Switzerland (dating from 1970) and declared stocks on the Nymex and Tocom futures exchanges.  Excluded are stocks held by governments (including Russia), producers, refiners and fabricators and consumers._ 

|**Implied stocks**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Platinum:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|1.86|2.22|2.87|3.29|
|Demand cover(months)|2.9|4.0|5.0|5.1|
|**Palladium:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|7.67|8.61|9.40|10.16|
|Demand cover(months)|11.0|13.8|13.8|13.5|



- Over the next three years platinum’s demand cover is expected to rise from around three months at the end of 2008 to approximately five months in 2010 and 2011.  This dispels the risk of a liquidity squeeze in platinum and suggests there is latitude for new ETF investment in existing and/or new funds. 

- For palladium, above‐ground stocks are forecast to remain substantial over the forecast period at significantly more than one year’s demand cover.  Although gross deficits across the forecast period will be a drain on global stock levels, holdings in the areas we measure (which exclude Russia) are expected to rise as transfers from Russian state holdings continue to enter the market. 

- _Note: forecast sales of palladium from Russian state stocks are included as inflows to implied above‐ground stocks in Switzerland.  These inclusions serve to inflate stocks in Switzerland but are balanced by commensurate declines in Russia’s state

owned inventories._
